clue.text: Where academics relax with copy of "The Predicament"

blocks.note: the senior common room, the staff lounge of an Oxbridge college
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Dons unwind in their lounge with a copy of a book called The Predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR, the senior common room, is where college fellows relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a scrape means being in an awkward fix or tight spot of trouble.

clue.text: Support that's thoroughly clean holding copper up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word for copper is read from bottom to top
one word holding another wraps around it on both sides

blocks.note: to scour is to scrub thoroughly
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A support strut that has been scrubbed down still holds up a copper fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help or assistance given in time of need, a synonym for support.

blocks.note: compost is matter left to rot down
OR introduces an alternative, coming after the thing it is an alternative to

explanation.surface: What the painter Turner might have used instead of manure.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner; here it is simply a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, such as helicopter blades, so it is literally something that turns.

definitions.note: adjective meaning relating to Passover, clued by an adverbial phrase

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something inside, so the mathematician swallows the other letter

blocks.note: Blaise Pascal, the French mathematician
the head, or first letter, of hog

explanation.surface: A mathematician breaks the Passover rules by downing a hogshead of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A hogshead is a large cask, but here it means the head of the word hog.
explanation.definitionFit: Paschal describes things belonging to the Jewish Passover or to Easter, such as the paschal lamb.

blocks.note: g is the symbol for gravitational force
an ambit is a scope or field of action

explanation.surface: A plan of attack that needs a force field, like a science-fiction battle tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move or calculated ploy, especially in chess, so a strategy or tactic.

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has been studying how investments increase in value.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital growth reads as finance; capital here means of the head, as in capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An antler is a bony outgrowth from a deer's head, and capital can mean relating to the head.

clue.text: Save revolutionary socialist from being massacred

blocks.note: save and but both mean except
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: Rescue a left-wing rebel before he is slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: Save looks like a verb meaning rescue; it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchered means slaughtered brutally and in large numbers, the same as massacred.

clue.text: Rock 'n' roller to fall in, getting drilled

indicators.note: in places the second word inside the first

blocks.note: a Teddy boy, the 1950s rock 'n' roll fan in Edwardian-style dress
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A rock 'n' roll dancer is told to line up and gets put through drill.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall in is a parade-ground order, but in is the container signal. A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a British 1950s youth who loved rock 'n' roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilled and trained both describe being taught by repeated practice and instruction.

clue.text: Updating original sin in reasonable quantities

indicators.note: original here means made new or novel, so the letters take a fresh order
in puts the shuffled letters inside the longer phrase

blocks.note: moderation is taking things in reasonable amounts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bringing the idea of original sin up to date by allowing it in moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: Original sin is a set theological phrase, so original hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Modernisation is the process of bringing something up to date, which is what updating means.

indicators.note: turned means the letters face the other way round

blocks.note: TUC's: the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions

explanation.surface: The trade union congress has turned tail and retreated.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the national body of British trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

blocks.note: surface reading: government ministers drawing lots and one picking the bad option
setter's reading: drawing lots with straws, the loser is the one who picks the shortest; Jack Straw was a senior Labour minister at the time

explanation.surface: Cabinet members draw lots and someone loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition; Jack Straw was Home Secretary then Foreign Secretary, adding a pun on ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever draws the shortest stalk when lots are drawn gets the unwanted task, so it is the unlucky pick.

indicators.note: in places the turn inside the river

blocks.note: the Forth, the Scottish river flowing past Edinburgh
a U-turn, so U is a turn

explanation.surface: A quarter turn made by a boat on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth is one of four equal parts of a whole, which is exactly a quarter.

clue.text: Mnemonist recalls legendary footballer and hard worker

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Pelé, the Brazilian football great
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A memory expert remembers a famous footballer and a diligent labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Recalls tempts as a memory link to Mnemonist, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially an elephant never forgets, so the animal is a playful name for someone with a great memory.

clue.text: Get a grip, seizing backside and doubling up

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the first word closes around the second

blocks.note: to cling is to grip tightly
the rump is the buttocks

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a bottom and collapses in laughter or pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Get a grip sounds like an order to calm down; here it means to hold tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpling describes folding or collapsing in on oneself, bent over as when doubling up.

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the wind wraps around the metal

blocks.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A specialist in winds is bagging some silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Magistral is an old adjective meaning masterly or authoritative, like a master or skilled authority.

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: crude oil is unrefined

explanation.surface: Raw, unprocessed muck that is mostly unrefined.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is slang for dirt, grime or any disgusting sticky deposit.

blocks.note: first meaning: silences, as when putting a cloth over a mouth
second meaning: jokes

explanation.surface: The censor cuts the jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag the press is to stop it speaking, and gags are also comedians' jokes.

clue.text: Architect King George I kept in work

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside the other word

blocks.note: Georgius Rex, King George
an opus is a work
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fitting King George I into a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: George I reads as a single monarch, but the numeral is the letter placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Gropius was the German architect who founded the Bauhaus school of design.

clue.text: A second volume about Stewart's sporting venue

indicators.note: about means around, so the book encloses the singer's name

blocks.note: taken as written
s is the abbreviation for second
a tome is a large book or volume
Rod Stewart, the rock singer

explanation.surface: A sequel book about a famous person's sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astrodome in Houston was the first domed sports stadium, an arena for baseball and football.

clue.text: Gemstone with 60% beryl content is pretty tough

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word keeps only its first three letters
a stone whose content is something holds that thing inside it

blocks.note: a ruby is a red gem
beryl is a mineral, the family of emerald

explanation.surface: A gem made largely of beryl is fairly hard-wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbery food or material is chewy and resistant, so somewhat tough to bite or break.

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped in, so the partner word goes around

blocks.note: a mate is a partner
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Something additional is included under one's spouse's permission.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or the authority given to act, so an authorisation.

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
arson is the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: Discreetly sacking the person currently holding the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Firing suggests dismissal; it means setting alight. An incumbent is also the holder of a Church of England parish.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England the incumbent is the priest holding a parish living, such as a vicar or rector.

clue.text: Unremitting claptrap on the way in

indicators.note: in places the following pair inside the word for nonsense

blocks.note: cant is insincere or hypocritical talk
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Nonstop rubbish being talked on the journey in.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means continuous and never letting up, which is what unremitting describes.

clue.text: Take time to feel at home

blocks.note: first meaning, split as two words
second meaning: be comfortable and accepted in a place

explanation.surface: It can take a while to settle in somewhere new.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense only works when the answer is split as be long.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to fit in naturally somewhere, being comfortable and accepted in that place.

clue.text: Fabric that's fairly crass, but not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely tells us only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A material that is rather tasteless, though not wholly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic material, a brand of elastane used in sportswear.

indicators.note: comic means funny or ludicrous, so the letters are jumbled up

blocks.note: taken as written
the indicator word's own letters join the fodder

explanation.surface: A brief study of humorous writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Comic serves twice: as the anagram signal and as part of the letters, making the clue a composite anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope examines the very tiny, so it investigates the minute, read as my-NEWT.

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
raw weather is bitterly cold

explanation.surface: A chill in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The craw is the crop or stomach of a bird or animal, hence the belly.

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the abbreviation faces the other way

blocks.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought in a letter
lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A note added late about the cloth used for bandaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid strip strapped to a broken limb to hold it still while it heals.

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the fireplace

blocks.note: a grate is the iron frame holding a fire
read as pony tail: the tail, or final letter, of pony

explanation.surface: Someone spinning a ponytail beside the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: Ponytail is one word but splits into pony and tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or whirl round in circles, the same as twirl.
